summary: A Thai costume rental and portrait session around Wat Arun pairs a memorable temple visit with traditional dress, accessories and optional hair, makeup or photographer. Shops operate independently near the temple exit; this is not a single temple-run activity. One named operator currently lists three-hour rentals from ฿300, while Wat Arun admission is separately listed by the Tourism Authority of Thailand at ฿200 for foreign adults. Allow extra time for ferry/temple queues, changing and photos. Prices, availability and shop terms may change before December 2026.
whyGo: Wear a Thai-style outfit for portraits against Wat Arun’s distinctive riverside prang.
Build the photoshoot into a temple visit; rental includes accessories at the cited shop.
bestFor: Visitors who enjoy posed portraits and are comfortable wearing elaborate clothing in public.
Couples, families and solo travellers wanting a keepsake from a Bangkok temple visit.
skipIf: You dislike crowds, heat, changing clothes, or being photographed in a busy public place.
You need step-free access or a guaranteed accessible changing and photography route; this could not be confirmed.
duration: Plan around 2–3 hours for changing, a temple visit and photos. Bestie Thai Costume lists rentals as three hours; photographer time and queues may add time.
cost: At Bestie Thai Costume’s currently published prices: standard costume ฿300, premium ฿600, deluxe ฿1,000 and exclusive ฿1,500 for three hours; optional hair and makeup cost extra. Its FAQ lists daily rental at an additional ฿700 plus a refundable ฿3,000 deposit (standard costumes only), differing from the price-list page’s ฿1,000 additional fee. Wat Arun entry is currently ฿200 for foreign adults per TAT; confirm both amounts before committing. Photographer pricing is quoted separately.
hours: Wat Arun: daily 08:00–18:00 per TAT. Bestie Thai Costume currently lists daily shop hours 08:45–17:30. December 2026 holiday operations should be reconfirmed.
bestTime: Arrive near opening for cooler temperatures and fewer visitors, then take photos before the temple gets busier. The operator says the site is crowded daily. Late afternoon offers softer light but leaves less time before closing; avoid assuming sunset photography can continue after temple hours.
gettingThere: From MRT Sanam Chai, go to Tha Tien Pier and take the cross-river ferry to Wat Arun; the temple’s map page reports departures roughly every 10–15 minutes. Chao Phraya Express Boat also serves Wat Arun Pier. Confirm pier and service on the day. Costume shops sit around Wang Doem Road by the temple exit.
booking: Walk-in rental may be possible, but a photographer is not guaranteed: Bestie says pre-booked guests receive its professional photographers and walk-ins are assigned whoever is waiting. It requests bookings 48 hours ahead. Contact the operator directly to confirm December date, package, photography price, deposit/payment terms, sizes and exact return time; no booking is made here.
accessibility: No reliable step-free route or accessible changing facilities were found in the sources. The temple complex includes outdoor paths and stairs around the prang; confirm current route and mobility support directly with the temple and rental shop. The cited shop says it has free lockers.
practicalTips: Wear breathable clothes and shoes that are easy to remove for changing; bring a small bag for valuables.
Dress respectfully at the temple, and ask staff before posing in restricted or active worship areas.
Confirm the costume’s rental clock, included accessories, deposit, photo delivery and the shop’s conflicting whole-day fee before paying.
Bring cash; the cited shop says card, WeChat and Alipay incur a 7% fee.
decemberNotes: December is a popular, relatively cooler Bangkok travel period, so reserve photographer and outfit in advance and expect crowds. No verified December 2026 temple event schedule was found. The temple and rental services may adjust operations for holidays; recheck shortly before the visit.
uncertainties: Current operator rates and conditions are not a guarantee for December 2026; its FAQ and price list conflict on the whole-day surcharge (฿700 vs ฿1,000).
TAT currently states ฿200 admission for foreign adults; confirm the gate price at visit time.
Photographer package prices, accessibility details and December holiday hours remain unconfirmed.
